t.E431.agn: In 1973 JECFA set an ADI of 0–25 mg/kg body weight per day for polyoxyethylene (8) and (40) stearates combined.
t.E431.body: In humans the polyoxyethylene (40) part is absorbed very little: only 2.3–3.1% was excreted in urine and 90–97% in faeces. The stearic acid part is largely (about 96%) digested.
t.E431.eval: The fatty acid source may be vegetable or animal (including beef/pork); the source is often not stated on the label.
t.E431.found.0: Included in the EU list of additives (Annex II Part B), but in the current consolidated text (18.08.2026) it is not authorised for use in any food category
t.E431.prod: It is produced by reacting stearic acid with polyoxyethylene (an ethylene oxide chain).
t.E431.regx.0: ADI of 0–25 mg/kg body weight for polyoxyethylene (8) and (40) stearates combined.
t.E431.regx.1: Named in the list of additives, but no conditions of use are defined for any food category (consolidated text 18.08.2026).
t.E431.summary: A synthetic emulsifier. In the EU it is not authorised for use in food.
t.E431.what: It is an emulsifier containing polyoxyethylene that allows oil and water to mix.
